title: test(plugin-timeline): return the array the readiness predicate accepted
body:
Fixes #7466

## Verdict first

**The failure is shape 2 (async settlement), it reproduces on demand, and it is already closed on `main` — not by anything in this PR, but by objectui#7527, which landed ~10 hours after #7466 was filed.** This PR claims no fix for the reported red. What it lands is the one thing the measurement showed was still resting on a single leg.

⚠️ **`main` is not a live defect.** Do not read this PR as "the flake is fixed"; read it as "the flake was already fixed, here is the proof it is, and here is the leg that was load-bearing without a guard of its own."

## The mandated loop reading, and why the first one was worthless

The card's own standard: run the file repeatedly, report failures/total.

```
pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-timeline/src/ObjectTimeline.colorFieldLadder-7243.test.tsx
```

| tree | runs | failures |
|:--|--:|--:|
| `main`, unperturbed, N=32 at concurrency 4 | 32 | **0** |
| pre-#7527 harness, same loop | 32 | **0** |

The second row is the point. The loop returns 0/32 on the tree that is *known* to carry the defect, so 0/32 on `main` measures nothing at all. Reporting the first row alone would have been the exact error the card warns about — treating a green run as evidence. **Not reproduced by repetition.**

## Establishing the mechanism

Instrumenting the pre-#7527 file to log every write to `lastItems` gave the reason: **one write per `colorsFor` call.** The late second write that the whole failure depends on never happens in this container.

`ObjectTimeline`'s data effect lists `objectDef` in its deps, and a *separate* `getObjectSchema()` sets `objectDef`. A mount therefore paints **once** if the two settle together and **twice** if they do not. This container settles them together; a loaded CI runner does not. So the lever is the **metadata fetch**, not machine load — and holding `getObjectSchema` by 25ms in the fixture splits them and makes the second paint appear.

Under that lever, everything becomes deterministic and discriminating:

| tree | perturbation | runs | failures |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|
| pre-#7527 harness | `getObjectSchema` +25ms | 3 | **3** |
| this file, as on `main` | `getObjectSchema` +25ms | 6 | 0 |
| `main` minus `unmount()` + DOM guard (token predicate alone) | `getObjectSchema` +25ms | 8 | **3** |
| ... plus this PR's bound capture | `getObjectSchema` +25ms | 16 | 0 |

Row 1 is the card's exact signature, at the second await of rung 2:

```
FAIL packages/plugin-timeline/src/ObjectTimeline.colorFieldLadder-7243.test.tsx:123
  > rung 2: 3- and 6-digit hex literals pass through
AssertionError: expected [ '#abc' ] to deeply equal [ '#123456' ]
- Expected
+ Received
  [
-   "#123456",
+   "#abc",
  ]
```

⇒ **Shape 2 confirmed. Shape 1 was never in play** — every run above uses the shared ladder unmodified, and `createFieldColorResolver` is a pure function of `value`. `packages/core/src/utils/record-color.ts` is untouched by this PR and no cache key was looked for or changed.

## What this PR actually changes, and why row 3 justifies it

Rows 3 and 4 are the same tree; the only difference is this diff.

`colorsFor` validated `lastItems` **inside** the `waitFor` predicate and then read the module-level global a **second time** on the next line. Those are two questions, and the second is asked after React's `act` yields to the macrotask queue on its way out of `waitFor` — a real window in which a still-live writer can answer it. Today that never bites, because `unmount()` has removed every other writer. But that makes the author-identifying predicate depend on a *different* guard to be sound: strip `unmount()` and the predicate alone fails **3/8**.

Binding the capture makes the value asserted and the value validated the same object by construction:

```ts
let settled: typeof lastItems = [];
await waitFor(() => {
  const items = lastItems;
  expect(items.map((i) => i.title)).toEqual(stampedRows.map((r) => r.subject));
  settled = items;
});
return settled.map((i) => i.color);
```

Same tree, **3/8 to 0/16**.

⛔ **No cheap exit is used.** No `retry`, no `sleep`, no widened timeout, no quarantine, and the two consecutive awaits in rung 2 — the only call sequence that exposes this — are untouched. The `it` blocks are **not** split.

## Ablation, anchored at this branch's commit

Run against `4f43a11fc` (implementation committed first, so the restore leg points at a HEAD that contains it). Each leg proved its mutation landed on disk by blob hash plus anchored `grep` counts, and restored under `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with restoration proved **by state** (`git hash-object` == the HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty), never by an exit code.

| leg | mutation | runs | failures |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|
| A | perturbation + strip `unmount()`/DOM guard + **revert this PR's capture** | 8 | **2** |
| B | perturbation + strip `unmount()`/DOM guard, capture intact | 16 | 0 |

## Header record

The numbers are written into the file's header on purpose. On an idle machine **every** variant above is green, so the next cleanup that reaches for one of these guards will find a passing run and no reason to keep it. The header gives it the lever and the failure rates instead.

## Verification — union re-run at `4f43a11fc`, clean tree

Exit codes captured by redirecting first, never through a pipe; each gate quoted from its own verdict line.

```

                                         declares 1 changeset(s): .changeset/7466-timeline-colorfieldladder-settlement.md.
                                         Every one of them has an EMPTY frontmatter — declared as releasing
                                         nothing, which is the explicit exemption and a complete answer to this gate.

check-changeset-fixed        EXIT=0  ✅  All workspace packages are in the changeset fixed group.
```

The changeset gate's BEFORE reading, for the record: `EXIT=1`, `❌ 1 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change adds no changeset`. The empty-frontmatter form is what the gate itself names as the pass for a test-only diff.

**Typecheck really covered the edited file** — `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` lists it (1 hit), so `EXIT=0` is a measurement and not a `**/*.test.ts` exclusion.

### Lint scope, declared

The repo-wide `eslint .` is CI's run. What is reported here is a **proved narrowing**, all three legs: ① the universe comes from eslint's own config resolution, not a guess — `eslint .` inside `packages/plugin-timeline` reports **27 files**; ② the count is read from `--format json`; ③ this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict, because `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService`, so linting is not type-aware and every file's result is a function of its own bytes plus a config this PR does not touch.
